findings.reason: the author must either reconcile the comment-based and card-based landings on one recogniser or state in the section why they are distinct questions, before putting a second one beside the first.
findings.text: §18 hoists the comment-based outstanding-sections reader into `reckon/_store.py`, but that module already owns the card-based landed-section recogniser `landed_section_ids(html_text)` (used by `plan_review.plan_fingerprint` at plan_review.py:425), and §18 names neither it nor the relation between the two notions of "landed"; two disjoint definitions of a landed section placed in one module drift apart and a reader cannot tell which question each answers

findings.reason: the author must move or reconcile the landing-comment notion and its prefix as part of the hoist, rather than forking a function whose dependency stays behind in another layer.
findings.text: §18 hoists `_plan_remaining_sections` (promotion.py:7236) to `_store.py`, but that reader depends on `_landed_sections` and its `_LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX = "c-run-"`, which already duplicates `plan_review.RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX` (plan_review.py:123); moving the reader alone leaves the hoisted `_store.py` public function importing the crew layer for a constant that has a core owner

findings.reason: keep the public function returning the one current digest and hold the form selection (current, pre-collapse, present whole-document) inside `_fingerprint_forms` or a private sibling, so the interface the call sites use does not grow.
findings.text: §16 turns `plan_fingerprint(plan, *, legacy: bool)` into a three-valued named mode, yet every production caller passing a flag is the private `_fingerprint_forms` (plan_review.py:603) and the ~30 remaining call sites pass nothing; the multi-form set already has its single home, so widening the public function's signature adds surface over machinery the private helper owns

findings.reason: either make the predicate module-private (keeping `public_definitions` flat) or add the one line §18 already carries stating why a cross-module reader needs a public name.
findings.text: §16 adds a public coverage predicate "the gate and the sweep read", but both consumers live in `reckon/crew/` alongside `plan_review.py`, unlike §18 which explicitly justifies its public home as the price of a cross-module mechanism; the section states why nothing is retired yet not why the new definition cannot be module-private

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the section-set fingerprint widens the public `plan_fingerprint` signature to a three-valued mode that only the private `_fingerprint_forms` consumes, spreading one concept across two interfaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 adds a second "which sections are still work" mechanism to `reckon/_store.py`, which already owns a landed-section recogniser, and the plan does not name it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds a public coverage definition whose consumers (the gate and the sweep) sit in the same `reckon/crew/` package and does not state why it cannot be module-private.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the owners it extends: §17 names `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py` and the store's `_section_heading`/`_section_body_end`, §18 names `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` and `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`, and §16 names `plan_fingerprint`/`_authored_prose`/`landed_section_ids`, so no scanner or reader is proposed where one exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (it joins a set of outstanding sections to the union of stored digests) and §17 extends the existing raw-text parser rather than adding a scanner, each with the honest-change justification the item asks for.
